title: Refactor CI stages: add weighted-lint-allocator and lockfile-gardener
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a weighted lint scheduling layer for presubmit lanes and a lockfile gardener that stages seed rotations for dependency updates. No public API changes. Improves CI feedback latency and reduces flakiness caused by oversized lint shards.
description: Motivation: our presubmit lint/test lanes have grown uneven: a small set of files cause huge lint jobs while other PRs run many trivial linters. This increases CI queue time and raises flake surface area. Separately, dependency roll PRs were frequently failing due to lockfile churn and noisy CI; locks were updated piecemeal which created transient regressions. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) weighted-lint-allocator: a scheduler component that assigns presubmit lint workers by historical file-cost weights (measured by average lint runtime and rule density). The allocator creates lightweight fast-lanes for small-surface changes and reserves heavy-lane slots for large or high-cost patches, enabling faster feedback for most PRs. 2) lockfile-gardener: a small orchestration service that performs atomic lock rotations for grouped dependency updates. It stages changes in a temporary branch, runs the CI matrix with a deterministic job ordering and retries only the failing matrix targets before opening the final roll PR. The gardener reduces non-deterministic lock churn and makes dep rotators (dependabot-like bots) more robust. Changes: - new package ci/allocator with: - weighting model (historical sampling + decay) - fast/normal/heavy lane selector - integration shim for GitHub Actions presubmit router - small opt-in config per repo in .github/ci-lanes.yaml - new package infra/lockfile-gardener with: - batch rotation runner - deterministic job ordering and selective retry logic - test harness that simulates the matrix and lockfile merge conflicts - new GH Action composite steps: ci/allocator-action and gardener-check - updates to main presubmit workflow to call allocator before lint shards and to gate dep-rolls through gardener - tests: unit tests for weighting functions, integration smoke tests that run a trimmed CI matrix using mocked runners - docs: README describing config knobs, migration guide, and operational runbook Checklist: - [x] design doc: ENG-1987 (linked) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] migration guide + config schema - [x] smoke deployment to staging CI cluster - [x] rollout plan with canary on small repos Rollout plan: stage behind a feature flag set in .github/ci-lanes.yaml. Start with two low-traffic repos, monitor average presubmit latency (SLO target: 75th percentile +15% improvement) and flakiness rate. For lockfile-gardener, run in dry-run mode for two weeks before enabling automatic PR creation. Related: ENG-1999 (release automation improvements), SUP-4421 (customer dep-rotation incident). Links: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1987 https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1999 Implementation notes: - The allocator stores lightweight per-path statistics in an internal Redis namespace; stats have TTL and decay to avoid stale weights. - We intentionally keep the initial weighting model simple (exponential moving average of observed lint runtimes per file, plus a per-rule penalty) to avoid RL-style complexity during rollout. - The gardener uses a two-step commit approach: create a staging branch, run the matrix, perform targeted retries for failures, then squash-merge the lock updates when the matrix stabilizes. Observability: Added metrics and dashboards: ci.allocator.job_latency_bucket, ci.allocator.shard_size, gardener.rolls.created, gardener.rolls.success_rate. Alerts: gardener:err_rate > 3% over 1h, allocator:queue_latency_p50 > 30s on presubmit lane. Security: gardener accesses repo tokens with limited scope (contents:write, checks:write) and records all operations to audit logs. Migration: repository owners opt-in by adding .github/ci-lanes.yaml with minimal config. Compatibility: backward compatible; default behavior if config absent remains current presubmit routing. Backwards impact: none.
commits: 6 commits: 1) add allocator core + weighting tests; 2) GH Action wrapper for allocator; 3) add lockfile-gardener core + matrix harness; 4) presubmit workflow hooks; 5) docs and runbook; 6) address reviewer feedback (win runner fixes + additional retries)
review_comments: Diego Morales (requested changes): The allocator looks promising but I worry about cold-start skew for new files. Please add a fallback that keeps file weight bounded until we observe at least N samples (N=3). Also add a unit test that validates decay behavior.
Maya Chen (author): Added bounded-initialization with N=3 and added decay unit tests in weights_test.go. Pushed commit 5 to address this.
Priya Singh (comment): The gardener's token scope should be minimal. Please confirm tokens don't grant admin rights and add a note to the runbook.
Maya Chen (author): Confirmed and updated runbook; gardener uses a deploy key with only contents:write and checks:write. See runbook section Operational Security.
Evelyn Hart (approval): Verified staging runs. Observed ~22% reduction in median lint job latency for the two pilot repos. Approve after small Windows runner fix.
Maya Chen (author): Fixed Windows runner shell escaping and re-ran staging; CI green. Pushed final squash commit for merge.

notes: This PR intentionally keeps the ML/complex weighting for a later phase; current approach is deterministic and easy to reason about. We expect to iterate on lane thresholds during the canary. Also added a small CLI helper for backfilling historical weights when migrating large repos.
